key_insight: People judge AI agents by more than whether they finish tasks: they also care about values like autonomy, dependability, affordability, bounded reach, reviewability, and equitable access. This paper shows that value-sensitive analysis of real user posts can reveal what users actually expect from everyday AI delegation.
problem_solved: Traditional evaluations of autonomous AI agents focus on task success, but miss the human values users care about when delegating work. This paper addresses the gap between technical performance metrics and value-based user experience.
method: Analyzed 73,093 first-person Reddit posts about OpenClaw using Value Sensitive Design.
Used LLM assistance to code each post for human value, agent aspect, value fulfillment, and user outcome.
Synthesized 21 values into 6 value groups to identify recurring user priorities and concerns.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical framework for evaluating agents beyond accuracy and completion rate. It can help teams design systems that are not only capable, but also more aligned with user trust, control, affordability, and fairness.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing Reddit posts flowing through value-sensitive coding into six value groups.
A grouped bar chart comparing the frequency of the 21 values across user experiences.
An icon-based dashboard for the six value groups: autonomy, dependability, affordability, bounded reach, reviewability, and equitable access.
A matrix or heatmap linking agent behaviors to user values and outcomes.
paper_title: Value-Sensitive Delegation in Everyday AI Agent Use: Evidence from OpenClaw
paper_authors: Renkai Ma, Ruyuan Wan, Xuan Lu, Fan Yang, Chen Chen
